grades.quote: A process that needs more memory at run-time (perhaps for malloc) can call sbrk(n) to grow its data memory by n zero bytes; sbrk returns the location of the new memory.
grades.reason: Provides basic sbrk semantics, but does not explain SBRK_LAZY, deferred physical allocation, or first-access behavior.

grades.quote: Xv6 uses the physical memory between the end of the kernel and PHYSTOP for run-time allocation. It allocates and frees whole 4096-byte pages at a time.
grades.reason: Provides background on physical allocation granularity, but not lazy address-space growth or first-access handling.

grades.quote:
Write a user program that grows its address space by one byte by calling sbrk(1). Run the program and investigate the page table for the program before the call to sbrk and after

the call to sbrk.
grades.reason: Suggests examining sbrk's allocation and page-table effects, but supplies no explanation of lazy allocation or first access.

grades.quote: Note that Xv6 uses a process’s page table not just to tell the hardware how to map user virtual addresses, but also as the only record of which physical memory pages are allocated to that process.
grades.reason: Provides auxiliary context about tracking physical backing through page tables, but does not explain SBRK_LAZY or first-access faults.
